title: The lazy monk
hookLine: a legend: Shantideva, thought lazy, is asked to recite, and recites a masterpiece

lines: A MONK WHO SEEMS TO DO NOTHING.
cards: A busy house can have one person who never seems to do anything. At the great monastery of Nalanda, the legend says, that person was a young monk named Shantideva.
The others saw him eat, sleep and wander, and never study, and tradition says they gave him a teasing nickname for it.
So they hatched a plan to embarrass him into leaving: invite him to give a public recitation, in front of everyone, and let him fail.

teach.b: In the Tibetan telling, the monks set up a high teaching seat, some say on purpose without steps, and gathered a crowd. Shantideva arrived, settled onto the seat without trouble, and asked a calm question.
Shall I recite something old, or something new? They asked for something new, expecting nothing.
And he began the Bodhicharyavatara, the Way of the Bodhisattva: verses on the joy of the awakening mind, on patience, on effort, on meditation, on wisdom. The crowd went quiet.
The lazy one spoke, and out came a masterpiece. Then the vanishing.

teach.h: HE RISES, AND HIS VOICE GOES ON.
teach.b: The legend says that when he reached the chapter on wisdom, at the verse where neither something nor nothing remains before the mind, he rose into the air and disappeared from sight, while his voice went on reciting.
His work was gathered afterward from those who had heard it. Nobody had known what was going on inside him.
Quiet isn't the same as empty. And that fits the week behind us. Aryadeva, the student who carried it.
Asanga, whose eyes compassion opened. Vasubandhu, who changed his mind. Yogacara and the mind that colors everything.
Logic asking how you know. Buddhaghosa's map. And now a monk everyone had judged, wrongly.

how: Shantideva's Way of the Bodhisattva is studied and recited in Tibetan Buddhism, and teachers tell the legend of his recitation at Nalanda when introducing the text.

practice: Bring to mind someone you may have quietly written off, a coworker who seems checked out, a relative who never says much, and picture them with whole rooms inside them that you've never seen.
Then let one small, kind surprise for them take shape, a thank-you, a real question, a bit of help, and rest with it.

wordCard.voice: Shantideva. The monk at Nalanda judged idle, who stood up and recited the Way of the Bodhisattva. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit name of the monk of the legend, who recited the Bodhicharyavatara.

carryVoice: Your line: the lazy one spoke. There may be a masterpiece you just haven't heard yet. That's the week, done.
